questions.q: What does Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) actually protect against?
options: Someone obtaining the physical data/log files or a backup file, without the certificate that protects the key
A DBA with sysadmin reading sensitive columns
Network traffic being sniffed between client and server
SQL injection attacks
questions.explain: TDE encrypts data at rest. A user with a legitimate login and permissions still reads the data normally once connected — TDE's threat model is a stolen disk or backup file.

questions.q: Why can even a sysadmin member not read an Always Encrypted column's plaintext by querying it directly?
options: The encryption keys never reach the SQL Server instance — only the client application can decrypt the values
sysadmin permissions don't include SELECT
Always Encrypted disables sysadmin automatically
The column is stored on a different server
questions.explain: Always Encrypted is client-side, column-level encryption; the decryption keys live outside SQL Server, so the instance (and anyone querying it directly, regardless of permissions) only ever sees ciphertext.

questions.q: What does connection encryption (TLS) protect that TDE and Always Encrypted do not?
options: Data in transit over the network between client and server
Data at rest in the physical data files
Specific columns from a DBA's view
Backup files from being restored elsewhere
questions.explain: TLS encrypts network traffic; TDE covers data at rest, and Always Encrypted covers specific columns even from someone with server access — the three are orthogonal, covering different threats.

questions.q: A compliance requirement says SSN data must be unreadable even to your own DBAs. Which technology satisfies that requirement?
options: Always Encrypted
TDE
TLS / connection encryption
None of these can satisfy that requirement
questions.explain: Only Always Encrypted keeps the decryption keys away from the SQL Server instance itself, so even a sysadmin querying the table sees ciphertext — TDE and TLS both still let an authorized login see plaintext.

questions.q: Which statement is true about TDE's effect on applications?
options: It's transparent — no query or connection-string changes are needed
Every query must be rewritten to decrypt columns explicitly
Applications must use a special TDE-aware driver
TDE requires Always Encrypted to also be enabled
questions.explain: TDE operates below the application layer, encrypting the physical files; applications and queries are unaffected and need no changes.
